Subject: Initial MAP + ask: Crestline private offer cadence

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our conversation I put together a lightweight stepchart (attached) to align procurement, finance, and engineering checkpoints so we can close the AWS private offer without surprises. High-level asks:

- Confirm the date Crestline needs production billing to start (we proposed Aug 1).
- Confirm PO approval path and typical sign-off lead times for your finance team.
- Share any required legal redline windows so our legal team can prioritize review.

Attachments: MAP_Crestline_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan); AWS_Private_Offer_Terms.pdf (template private-offer terms).

I sketched a 6-week timeline: evaluation sandbox (1 week), internal security checks (2 weeks), PO & legal (2 weeks), switch to billed environment + kickoff (1 week). If those durations look off for your internal process, tell me where to shorten/lengthen.

Next steps: can you confirm the procurement owner and best dates for a two-week window for finance approval? I’ll update the MAP and circulate.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@crestline.com>

Cc: procurement@crestline.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + ask: Crestline private offer cadence

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear note and attachments. Internal confirmation: I own procurement for this deal and will be the primary approver. Quick answers:

- Production billing target: we *can* do Aug 15 as a safe target (we prefer mid-month).
- PO approval path: procurement → legal review (up to 5 business days) → finance sign-off (typically 3 business days). Our calendar is light second week of July.
- Legal redlines: please send the private-offer terms to legal@crestline.com and CC me; they like a 3-business-day turnaround but sometimes ask for a week depending on scope.

I attached our internal procurement checklist (short). We really want SSO/SCIM proof and SOC2 evidence before final approval. Also confirm whether Redwood supports invoice net-30 or if you require immediate marketplace billing.

Best,
Anita Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager | Crestline Analytics
Attachments: CRESTLINE_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@crestline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, legal@crestline.com
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + ask: Crestline private offer cadence

Anita —

Appreciate the details. I updated the MAP (see attached MAP_Crestline_v1.xlsx -> tracked changes) with the timeline shifted to target Aug 15 for production billing. Key milestones (summary):

1) Week 1 (Jul 2–8): Evaluation sandbox access + sample dataset import.
2) Week 2 (Jul 9–15): Security intake (SSO/SCIM demo) + SOC2 attestation packet.
3) Week 3 (Jul 16–22): Partner legal & Crestline legal redlines (we’ll aim for 3 business-day turnaround).
4) Week 4 (Jul 23–29): PO issuance and AWS private-offer acceptance.
5) Week 5 (Jul 30–Aug 5): Billing switch verification in staging + finance confirmation.
6) Week 6 (Aug 6–15): Go-live and billed usage begins Aug 15.

Regarding invoice terms: Redwood offers both options depending on whether you want to flow through AWS Marketplace billing or a net-invoice route (we can accommodate net-30 on committed Dedicated contracts). I’ve noted this as a decision point in the MAP (Decision A: Marketplace billing vs. Net-30 invoiced by Redwood).

Docs & links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7832; DocuSign envelope (private offer): https://www.docusign.com/crestline/ENVELOPE-98234

Please review the updated MAP and let me know redline expectations from Crestline legal. Priyom — I’ve added you for billing path options and finance cadence.

Thanks,
Jordan
---

Looks good to me. Two quick items: please loop our Legal (legal@redwood.ai) on the private-offer packet before sending to Crestline legal; they can prioritize a 48–72 hour review if needed. Also, include Dedicated onboarding (onboard@redwood.ai) in the kickoff invite so we can reserve a slot for the production cutover.

+1 on making the Marketplace vs invoice decision explicit in the MAP.

—Laura
